chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār, who said:
Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام was asked about a well into which a basket of dry or moist excrement falls, and he said: There is no harm, if there is abundant water in it.

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: a well, the source of water under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.رَطْبَةٍ: moist or wet, describing the other state of the impurity
key_terms.زِنْبِيلُ: a basket, the container that fell into the well
key_terms.عَذِرَةٍ: excrement or filth, the impurity mentioned in the case
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm, indicating permissibility or absence of legal problem
key_terms.مَاءٌ كَثِيرٌ: abundant water, the condition upon which the ruling depends
key_terms.يَابِسَةٍ: dry, describing one state of the impurity

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a well if a basket of dry or wet excrement falls into it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a well into which a basket of excrement falls. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that there is no problem when the well contains abundant water, indicating the legal significance of water quantity in rulings of ritual purity.
